title: Influence and decision-tree revealment
statement: Let $\\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\\pi$ be a probability distribution assigning positive probability to every element of $\\Omega$, and let $\\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set with a chosen real orthonormal basis of functions on $\\Omega$ for the $\\pi$-weighted inner product, one basis vector being the constant-one function. For a nonconstant function $f:\\Omega^n\\to\\mathbb R$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$, its variance under the product distribution divided by its function revealment is at most its total influence under that product distribution.
hypotheses_covered: $\\pi$ is a probability distribution with full support
$\\iota$ is finite and nonempty and has decidable equality
There is a real basis of functions on $\\Omega$ indexed by $\\iota$, containing the constant-one vector and orthonormal for the $\\pi$-weighted inner product
